text:
jordan_support: Hey team — customer reported intermittent failures when their Private control plane agent tries to connect over mTLS. They see sporadic handshake failures ~1-2x/hour since last night. Stacktrace from the agent: `tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: handshake failure` and the agent logs show repeated `client_hello` then `alert` with no application data. Can we triage?

priya_eng: Thanks Jordan. Which control plane endpoint (hostname) and do we have a sample ClientHello? Also, did this start after any customer-side change (proxy/fw update)?

jordan_support: Endpoint: control.private.redwood.example.com:443. Customer says they rolled a small proxy update last night but claims it was a config tweak only (timeout bump). They attached a small packet capture of one failed attempt (pcap excerpt they sent). Snippet from tcpdump they provided: ```13:14:02.123456 IP client > cp: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 13:14:02.125678 client > cp: TLS Client Hello, length 512 (fragmented) 13:14:02.125689 cp > client: TLS Alert, length 2, level: fatal, description: handshake_failure```

sam_network: Quick look: that pattern (ClientHello then immediate Alert) often indicates either: (1) ALPN or SNI removed/modified by middlebox, (2) client and server couldn't agree on ciphers / TLS versions, or (3) ClientHello fragmentation causing proxy to drop/modify. Does the capture show TLS 1.3 ClientHello or TLS 1.2?

jordan_support: Customer's agent shows it uses Go TLS default (supports TLS1.3, TLS1.2), but their proxy does TLS inspection (corporate NGFW). In working attempts we see TLS1.3 ClientHello with ALPN = "h2,http/1.1" in the clear; in failing attempts the ALPN is missing in the capture and SNI looks truncated (ends mid-hostname).

priya_eng: Truncated SNI is a strong hint. Some inspection appliances have MTU/fragment reassembly bugs or apply HTTP/TLS rewriting that chops the ClientHello. Can the customer dump the full ClientHello hex? Ask for `openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.example.com:443 -tls1_3 -servername control.private.redwood.example.com -msg -alpn h2` output. That will show if the SNI is emitted properly from their agent box.

maria_sre: Also ask them to check for any transparent proxy or TCP MSS clamping on the path. If a middlebox drops TCP segments or fails to reassemble, the server sees incomplete ClientHello and responds with handshake_failure. Quick test: from the agent host run `curl --http2 -v https://control.private.redwood.example.com/healthz --resolve control.private.redwood.example.com:443:IP` and compare working vs failing runs.

oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-431 auto-created for repeated mTLS handshake failures (seen by support). Priority P2. Assigned: maria_sre.

sam_network: If customer can reproduce reliably, ask them to disable TLS inspection for that destination (whitelist control plane IPs) briefly. If failures stop, it's definitely a middlebox issue. If they can't disable, ask for a tcpdump with `tcpdump -w /tmp/mtls.pcap host control.private.redwood.example.com and port 443` and share the pcap via secure upload.

jordan_support: Customer replied — they can reproduce ~3/10 attempts. They tried whitelist and reported it dropped to 0/10 for ~30 minutes then came back. They provided two pcaps (working/failed). I uploaded both to the incident.

priya_eng: From the failed pcap I pulled the ClientHello bytes. SNI string ends with `control.private.redw` then a gap, then nothing. That looks like fragmentation inside the proxy. Workaround: ask them to increase TCP reassembly buffer on the NGFW or disable TLS inspection for the control plane FQDN/IP range. Long term: we should add guidance to Private install docs to require whitelisting of control plane FQDNs and document minimum TCP reassembly settings.

maria_sre: Agreed. Also check that their proxy isn't stripping ALPN; we've seen proxies that downgrade or remove ALPN leading to server choosing an unexpected codec and then closing. Quick reproducible command for them to run on the agent host to verify ALPN/SNI: ```openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.example.com:443 -servername control.private.redwood.example.com -alpn h2 -tls1_3 -msg``` Compare the ClientHello in both cases.

sam_network: Another possible angle: some NAT devices do port preservation but change packet segmentation. If the SNI crosses an MSS boundary and the proxy doesn't reassemble before inspection, the inspector sees truncated SNI. Ask for `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and MTU on the path.

jordan_support: Customer sent their NGFW model and a short vendor release note referencing a known bug "SNI fragmentation on TLS1.3 ClientHello when TLS inspection enabled" — looks like a vendor bug. They raised a case with their vendor, but asked if Redwood can support a temporary config change.

priya_eng: For short-term mitigation: 1) whitelist control plane IPs on the NGFW (egress allowlist) and bypass TLS inspection 2) allowlist our control plane IP CIDR(s) so traffic isn't proxied 3) if they can't whitelist, consider configuring the agent host to force TLS1.2 (not ideal) as a temporary test to avoid large ClientHello sizes. Command example to force TLS1.2 in agent: set environment var `GODEBUG=tls13=0` in a test run, or run openssl with `-tls1_2` to validate.

maria_sre: I'll update the incident with recommended customer-facing steps and request they share vendor case ID. Also we should add a short KB about this exact failure mode. Jordan — can you ask for: full pcap, NGFW config snippet showing TLS inspection profile, vendor case ID, and whether they can temporarily whitelist our control plane CIDR?

jordan_support: Sent checklist to customer. They replied: vendor case opened, they will try whitelist during their maintenance window (in 2 hours). I'll update here after their test.

oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-431 status updated: awaiting customer whitelist test.

priya_eng: Thanks — if the whitelist removes failures we mark root cause as NGFW ClientHello reassembly bug. Long term, add explicit note in Private onboarding: "Ensure TLS inspection bypass or reassembly buffer >= 64KB for control plane" and include sample allowlist rules.

maria_sre: Closing note: if customer cannot whitelist, we can offer a temporary dedicated endpoint (short lived IP) to be allowlisted while they engage vendor. But that's an ops decision — I'll loop in product if needed.

jordan_support: Customer confirmed after maintenance: whitelist applied, failures stopped (0/50). Vendor confirmed bug and scheduled firmware fix. Marking this thread as resolved for now, will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
